concerns.text: FR-005 and Principle VII name `network_flexibility` as the primary predictor; T106 fits `excess_flexibility` instead. The revision note admits this is 'a spec-level change' but the spec was never amended — the task list silently redefines the primary hypothesis test without spec authorization. Either amend FR-005 or fit the spec-named predictor.

FR-007 requires FWE correction 'across any multiple hypotheses tested (e.g., ROI-wise correlations)'. No task T101–T113 computes ROI-wise correlations or any multiple-hypothesis family, so T107's FWE step has no family to correct over — the FR is tagged as satisfied but is semantically unverifiable as planned.

Constitution VI mandates raw HCP releases under data/raw/ and requires any deviation to be 'documented in a provenance file and reflected in a new derived data artifact'. T102 fetches from an OpenNeuro mirror ('ds003189-style') with checksums only — no task writes the mandated provenance file documenting the deviation from the canonical HCP source, nor records software versions/args/atlas version as Principle VI requires.

Spec's power assumption targets ≈1000 HCP participants; T110 profiles only a 10-subject subset with 'projected' full-run runtime and no task reconciles the sampled-subject count with the >80% power claim. T112 mentions a 'power implication' caveat but the sample-size narrowing relative to the spec assumption is never justified in the task list.

data-model.md still states `code/utils/versioning.py` updates `state/projects/...yaml` with artifact hashes, contradicting the tasks.md ruling that no task writes to state/. T113's scope (file-table paths only) does not correct this stale constraint text, leaving the two artifacts in direct conflict.

T110 asserts SHA-256 checksums of `data/interim/*.csv` against `data/checksums.json`, but data-model.md defines that file as the registry for raw data files only. The tasks document silently widens the checksum registry's scope without updating the data model (T113 does not cover this).
